THE VALUE FOR YOUR BUSINESS

Less rekeying. Less reconciliation.
More control over every transaction.

After bind, teams still recreate insurance data in spreadsheets, reports and finance systems. Bordeon is being designed to remove that repeated work.

01 / CAPTURE ONCE

Stop entering the same risk twice.

Reuse one verified record across policies, endorsements, bordereaux and finance exports.

Less rekeying and fewer mismatched records.
02 / REPORT FROM THE RECORD

Prepare carrier reporting without rebuilding spreadsheets.

Generate each carrier’s required output from structured transaction data instead of assembling it again at reporting time.

Less bordereau preparation and a consistent source for every report.
03 / TRACE EVERY CHANGE

Know what changed. Know what is owed.

Link endorsements, premium adjustments and settlement obligations to the original policy, with its history preserved.

A clear audit trail and less investigation when amounts differ.
04 / KEEP YOUR EXISTING SYSTEMS

Connect insurance operations to finance.

Bring bound business into Bordeon and pass structured data downstream. Your CRM owns the relationship; your ERP owns the accounting.

Cleaner handovers without replacing your CRM or ERP.

Planned benefits to validate with design partners. Bordeon is in development.

HOW BORDEON WORKS

Business bound.
Transaction record established.

One canonical insurance transaction record. Multiple systems and formats.

  1. Bind
  2. Policy
  3. Endorsement
  4. Premium transaction
  5. Bordereau
  6. Settlement obligation
01 / BIND & CLOSING

Create the authoritative transaction record when business is bound.

Planned product scope. Submissions, underwriting, quoting and placement remain in upstream systems; invoicing, accounting and cash management remain downstream.

FOLLOW ONE CHANGE THROUGH THE BUSINESS

A higher insured value.
A complete transaction trail.

When the vessel’s value changes, the policy is not overwritten. A linked endorsement creates a premium adjustment, feeds the July bordereau and updates the carrier’s settlement obligation.

Received settlement information is then matched to those transactions. Bordeon records what is owed and why; the ERP handles invoicing, accounting and payments.

Illustrative marine example. The same transaction model is intended for other specialty lines. Premium and obligation amounts depend on contract terms and are not calculated in this prototype.

BUILT FIRST FOR EUROPEAN SPECIALTY MGAs

Complex bound business.
Multiple carriers.
One transaction layer.

Our initial focus is specialty MGAs and underwriting agencies managing bound business across multiple carriers, with policy changes, bordereaux and settlement obligations still dependent on spreadsheets and documents.

Brokers provide placement and closing information. Carriers receive reporting and transaction data. Finance teams keep their existing ERP and accounting workflows.

Bordeon is an early-stage platform concept. The starting point is post-bind operations; the longer-term ambition is interoperable infrastructure connecting MGAs, brokers and carriers across specialty lines.
